Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly‑rated and widely‑praised crime‑thriller films released in 2020. (All titles were released theatrically or on major streaming platforms during the calendar year.)

| # | Film | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern, tech‑savvy take on the classic horror story that doubles as a tense psychological thriller. Moss delivers a powerhouse performance as a woman who believes she’s being stalked by an unseen predator. |
| 2 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie’s signature fast‑paced, witty style shines in this heist‑drama about a British drug lord trying to sell his empire. The film balances sharp dialogue with a complex web of double‑crosses. |
| 3 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | Though more courtroom drama than pure crime‑thriller, the film’s tense, real‑time narrative and razor‑sharp dialogue capture the paranoia and conspiracies of the 1968 trial. |
| 4 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A chilling psychological thriller about a man who becomes the target of a violent mob hunt after a false accusation. The film’s claustrophobic tension and moral ambiguity make it unforgettable. |
| 5 | **The Night House** | David Bruckner | Rebecca Hall, Nathan Lane | A slow‑burn horror‑thriller that blends supernatural dread with a deeply unsettling exploration of grief and guilt. Hall’s performance anchors the film’s eerie atmosphere. |
| 6 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A historical crime‑thriller that dramatizes a medieval duel over a woman’s honor. The film’s gritty realism and strong performances keep viewers on edge. |
| 7 | **The Platform** | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Jorge García | A Spanish sci‑fi thriller that turns a vertical prison into a brutal social experiment. The film’s stark visuals and allegorical depth create a tense, claustrophobic experience. |
| 8 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern, tech‑savvy take on the classic horror story that doubles as a tense psychological thriller. Moss delivers a powerhouse performance as a woman who believes she’s being stalked by an unseen predator. |
| 9 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern, tech‑savvy take on the classic horror story that doubles as a tense psychological thriller. Moss delivers a powerhouse performance as a woman who believes she’s being stalked by an unseen predator. |
| 10 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern, tech‑savvy take on the classic horror story that doubles as a tense psychological thriller. Moss delivers a powerhouse performance as a woman who believes she’s being stalked by an unseen predator. |

> **Quick note:** The list above mixes pure crime‑thrillers with films that blend elements of psychological suspense, courtroom drama, and even horror. If you’re looking for a strictly “crime‑thriller” feel, focus on titles like *The Invisible Man*, *The Gentlemen*, and *The Hunt*.

Enjoy your binge‑watching!
